newsitem.title: USA: Disney signs Eisner to long-term contract.
newsitem.headline: Disney signs Eisner to long-term contract.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. Thursday signed Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Michael Eisner to a long-term contract, assuring he will remain at the helm of the entertainment giant through Sept. 30, 2006.
Disney also revealed that former president Michael Ovitz, who resigned last month, got $38.9 million in severance pay from the giant entertainment company.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Disney also said that a stock option for 3 million common shares became exercisable when Ovitz resigned on Dec. 27.
In a separate statement, Disney said Eisner's base salary would be $750,000 a year, the same rate since 1984, plus a new bonus tied to the company's financial performance.

Disney, which operates theme parks, film studios and television and radio stations, said the bonus formula is tied to the growth of the company's earnings per share above an annual threshold growth rate of 7.5 percent.

In addition, Eisner received a grant of stock options for 8 million shares of Disney stock. Of this grant, options for 5 million shares vest on Sept. 30, 2003, carrying a strike price of $63.3125 each. Three million shares in three equal instalments of one million shares each vest on Sept. 30, 2004, 2005, and 2006, carrying strike prices of 125 percent, 150 percent, and 200 percent of the strike price respectively.
The bonus formula for the new agreement will be submitted for stockholder approval at the company's stockholder meeting on Feb. 25.
Disney's stock closed down 62.5 cents at $67.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
